slides.heading: Semordnilap
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Strings
slides.narration: Let's solve Semordnilap, an easy strings problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Return pairs of distinct words where one is the reverse of the other.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Return pairs of distinct words where one is the reverse of the other.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: A word and its reverse form a pair; a hash set finds each partner in constant time.
slides.narration: A word and its reverse form a pair; a hash set finds each partner in constant time.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Brute force: compare every pair → O(n²·m)
Optimal: hash set of words → O(n·m)
slides.narration: Comparing every pair of words is quadratic. With a hash set, each word checks for its reverse in constant time, so the whole thing is linear in the total characters.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Put all words in a set
2. For each word, check whether its reverse is present and different
3. Record the pair and remove both
slides.narration: Step by step. First, put all words in a set. Second, for each word, check whether its reverse is present and different. Third, record the pair and remove both.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'diaper' ↔ 'repaid'
slides.narration: The reverse of diaper is repaid, which is in the set. Record the pair and remove both so it isn't counted twice.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'abc' ↔ 'cba'
slides.narration: The reverse of abc is cba, which is in the set. Record the pair and remove both so it isn't counted twice.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: 'tset' not present
slides.narration: The reverse of test, tset, isn't in the list.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We put all words in a set. For each word, we reverse it; if the reverse is in the set and differs from the word, we add the pair and remove both words.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n times m. Space is O of n times m.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Palindromes like 'aba' don't pair with themselves
Remove matched words to avoid duplicate pairs
slides.narration: A palindrome would match itself, so skip that case. Removing matched words prevents duplicate pairs.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
bullets: Follow-up: count pairs, or allow duplicates
slides.narration: Follow-ups include counting pairs or handling duplicate words.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: A word and its reverse form a pair; a hash set finds each partner in constant time.
slides.narration: To recap Semordnilap: A word and its reverse form a pair; a hash set finds each partner in constant time. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
